name: opensearch-migration-system

ground_truth.threatName: Man-in-the-Middle Attack via Traffic Capture Proxy

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: An attacker who gains access to the proxy could intercept traffic between the source and target clusters, potentially modifying requests/responses or extracting sensitive data.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the proxy's configuration or implementation to gain control, then intercepts and modifies OpenSearch queries or responses.

recommendations.description: Implement mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication between all components
recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure mTLS in the ALB and ECS services using ACM certificates. Update security groups to restrict traffic to TLS only.

recommendations.description: Enhance proxy access controls and monitoring
recommendations.implementationDetails: Implement WAF rules on ALB, enable AWS Shield Advanced, and configure detailed CloudWatch logging with alerts for suspicious patterns.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The CDK code shows the proxy is deployed as a Fargate task with basic security group rules. Enhanced security measures like WAF, Shield Advanced, and stricter security group rules should be implemented. The ALB should be configured with TLS termination and re-encryption.

ground_truth.threatName: Management Console Compromise via Web Vulnerabilities

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: An attacker exploits web vulnerabilities in the management console to gain unauthorized access, potentially leveraging cross-account IAM roles to access sensitive data.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: Attacker finds an SQL injection vulnerability in the console's authentication mechanism, gains admin access, and uses the console's legitimate cross-account access to exfiltrate data.

recommendations.description: Implement strict IAM policies with least privilege
recommendations.implementationDetails: Review and tighten the ECS task role permissions, implement session policies, and use AWS Organizations SCPs to enforce guardrails.
Implement WAF rules for common web attacks, enable AWS Shield Advanced, use AWS Secrets Manager for credentials, and implement robust input validation.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The CDK code shows broad IAM permissions in the mgmtConsolePolicy. These should be restricted using condition keys and resource-level permissions. WAF rules should be added to the ALB.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: An attacker with access to the MSK cluster could modify messages in Kafka topics, potentially altering the captured traffic before replay.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: Attacker gains access to MSK, modifies captured traffic to include malicious queries, which are then replayed to the target cluster.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable TLS encryption for MSK, implement SASL/SCRAM authentication, and add message signatures for integrity verification.
Use private subnets for MSK, implement strict security group rules, enable encryption at rest with KMS, and configure audit logging.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The CDK code shows MSK configured with basic security. Enable encryption at rest using KMS, configure TLS encryption in transit, and implement SASL/SCRAM authentication instead of IAM authentication for better security.

mitreATT&CK: T1537 - Transfer Data to Cloud Account

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Overly permissive IAM roles or resource policies could allow unauthorized access across account boundaries.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker compromises the migration account and exploits broad cross-account permissions to access data in source/target accounts.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use external IDs for cross-account role assumption, implement strict resource policies, and use AWS Organizations SCPs.
Enable AWS CloudTrail with organization trail, configure GuardDuty, and set up alerts for suspicious cross-account activity.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The CDK code shows basic cross-account role assumptions. Implement external IDs, condition keys for source IP restrictions, and time-bound access using aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition.

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Misconfigured S3 bucket policies or overly permissive IAM roles could allow unauthorized access to snapshot data.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: Attacker finds a misconfigured bucket policy that allows public access or exploits overly permissive IAM roles to access snapshots.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable default encryption with KMS, implement strict bucket policies, enable versioning, and configure access logging.
Use S3 Block Public Access, enable Amazon Macie for sensitive data discovery, and regularly audit bucket permissions.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The CDK code shows basic S3 bucket configuration. Enable default encryption with KMS CMK, implement strict bucket policies with condition keys, and enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
AWS OpenSearch Migration Assistant Architecture Diagram
This script generates an architecture diagram showing the components and workflow
of the AWS OpenSearch Migration Assistant using the diagrams package.
"""

# AWS Service imports
from diagrams.aws.network import ELB
from diagrams.aws.compute import ECS
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3
from diagrams.aws.analytics import Kinesis
from diagrams.aws.analytics import ES
from diagrams.aws.management import Cloudwatch
from diagrams.aws.security import Shield

# Generic imports
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge
from diagrams.generic.network import Firewall
from diagrams.generic.compute import Rack

# Custom graph attributes for different boundaries
migration_account_attr = {
    "style": "dashed",
    "bgcolor": "lightblue",
    "label": "Migration Account"
}

source_account_attr = {
    "style": "dashed",
    "bgcolor": "lightgreen",
    "label": "Source Account"
}

target_account_attr = {
    "style": "dashed",
    "bgcolor": "lightyellow",
    "label": "Target Account"
}

trust_boundary_attr = {
    "style": "dotted",
    "bgcolor": "lightgrey"
}

# Define diagram attributes
graph_attr = {
    "splines": "ortho",  # Use orthogonal lines for connections
    "nodesep": "0.8",    # Minimum space between nodes
    "ranksep": "1.0",    # Minimum space between ranks
    "pad": "2.0"         # Padding around the diagram
}

# Create the diagram
with Diagram(
    name="AWS OpenSearch Migration Assistant Architecture",
    filename="aws_opensearch_migration",
    direction="LR",  # Left to Right layout for better flow visualization
    show=True,
    graph_attr=graph_attr,
    outformat="png"
):
    # Migration Account Boundary
    with Cluster("Migration Account", graph_attr=migration_account_attr):
        # Migration Infrastructure with Trust Boundary
        with Cluster("Migration Infrastructure\nTrust Boundary", graph_attr=trust_boundary_attr):
            # Load Balancer and Proxy
            alb = ELB("Application\nLoad Balancer")
            proxy = Firewall("Traffic\nCapture Proxy")
            
            # Migration Management Console on ECS
            mgmt_console = ECS("Migration\nManagement Console")
            
            # Traffic Replayer
            replayer = Rack("Traffic\nReplayer")
            
            # Snapshot Storage
            snapshot = S3("Snapshot\nStorage")
            
            # Message Queue for captured traffic
            with Cluster("Amazon MSK"):
                kafka = Kinesis("Kafka Cluster")

    # Source Account Boundary
    with Cluster("Source Account", graph_attr=source_account_attr):
        with Cluster("Source Trust Boundary", graph_attr=trust_boundary_attr):
            source_cluster = ES("Source Cluster\n(OpenSearch)")

    # Target Account Boundary
    with Cluster("Target Account", graph_attr=target_account_attr):
        with Cluster("Target Trust Boundary", graph_attr=trust_boundary_attr):
            target_cluster = ES("Target Cluster\n(OpenSearch)")

    # Create CloudWatch monitoring in Migration Account
    with Cluster("Monitoring & Analysis", graph_attr=trust_boundary_attr):
        metrics = Cloudwatch("CloudWatch\nMetrics")
        logs = Cloudwatch("CloudWatch\nLogs")

    # Cross-Account Traffic Flow
    alb >> Edge(color="blue", label="Route Traffic") >> proxy
    proxy >> Edge(color="green", label="Forward Traffic", style="bold") >> source_cluster
    proxy >> Edge(color="orange", label="Capture Traffic") >> kafka

    # Cross-Account Migration Flow
    mgmt_console >> Edge(color="red", label="Initiate RFS", style="bold") >> source_cluster
    source_cluster >> Edge(color="red", style="dashed") >> snapshot
    snapshot >> Edge(color="red", style="bold") >> target_cluster
    
    # Traffic Replay Flow
    mgmt_console >> Edge(color="purple", label="Control") >> replayer
    kafka >> Edge(color="purple", style="dashed") >> replayer
    replayer >> Edge(color="purple", style="bold") >> target_cluster

    # Monitoring connections
    source_cluster >> Edge(style="dotted") >> metrics
    target_cluster >> Edge(style="dotted") >> metrics
    proxy >> Edge(style="dotted") >> logs
    kafka >> Edge(style="dotted") >> logs
    replayer >> Edge(style="dotted") >> logs
